body: Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service. It handles sign-in, single sign-on, self-service password reset and multifactor authentication for Microsoft cloud apps and apps you build. Microsoft Entra Connect syncs identities between on-premises Active Directory and Entra ID. Microsoft Entra Domain Services is different: it gives managed domain services (domain join, group policy, LDAP, Kerberos/NTLM) without you running domain controllers, which helps with legacy applications that cannot use modern authentication.
author: claude

body: Single sign-on (SSO) lets a user sign in once and reach many trusted applications. Multifactor authentication (MFA) asks for an extra factor, so a stolen password is not enough. The factors are something you know (a password), something you have (a phone code) and something you are (a fingerprint or face scan). Passwordless sign-in removes the password and uses a trusted device plus a biometric or PIN. Microsoft Entra ID supports Windows Hello for Business, the Microsoft Authenticator app and FIDO2 security keys.
author: claude

body: An external identity is a person, device or service that exists outside your tenant. Microsoft Entra External ID covers securely working with them. With B2B collaboration, external users sign in with their own preferred identity to reach your apps, and they usually appear in your directory as guest users. The external identity provider manages their authentication, while you manage what they are allowed to access. Microsoft Entra External ID for customers, formerly Azure AD B2C, is for publishing apps to consumers and customers.
author: claude

body: Conditional Access is a tool Microsoft Entra ID uses to allow or deny access based on identity signals. The signals include who the user is, where they are and what device they use. Conditional Access collects the signals, makes a decision, and enforces it by allowing access, blocking it, or asking for multifactor authentication. Common uses are requiring MFA for privileged roles or for people outside trusted networks, requiring managed devices, and blocking untrusted locations.
author: claude

body: Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) manages access to Azure resources by role instead of by person. Built-in roles include Owner, which has increased control, and Reader, which can only view. You can also define your own roles. A role is assigned at a scope: a management group, a subscription, a resource group or a single resource. Permissions granted at a parent scope are inherited by every child scope. Azure RBAC uses an allow model, so assignments add permissions and never deny them.
author: claude

body: Zero Trust is a security model that assumes breach from the start and verifies every request as if it came from an uncontrolled network. Its guiding principles are: verify explicitly, by authenticating and authorizing using all available data points; use least privilege access, with Just-In-Time and Just-Enough-Access; and assume breach, by limiting impact, segmenting access and using analytics to detect threats. Access depends on authentication, not on whether the user is inside the network.
author: claude

body: Defense in depth uses a series of layers to slow an attack and protect data, so if one layer is breached the next is already in place. The layers are physical security, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application and data. The perimeter layer uses DDoS protection, the network layer limits communication through segmentation, and the compute layer secures access to virtual machines. The data layer protects the information itself.
author: claude

body: Microsoft Defender for Cloud is a security posture management and threat protection service. It monitors cloud, on-premises, hybrid and multicloud resources and gives recommendations and alerts. It works in three areas: continuously assess your posture, secure resources against the Microsoft cloud security benchmark, and defend against threats. Recommendations are grouped into security controls and used to calculate a secure score that helps teams prioritize improvements. To cover on-premises machines you deploy Azure Arc.
author: claude
